You'll use data from the 2024 round of the General Social Survey to answer these questions. Scroll to @sec-codebook at the end of this document for some additional details on the variables you'll need to complete this analysis.

# Data import

You can download GSS data [directly from their website](https://gss.norc.org/us/en/gss/get-the-data.html), but Kieran Healy [has created an R package](https://kjhealy.github.io/gssr/) that will automatically import `GSS` data into R and provides some additional helper functions for working with the data.

Download the `gssr` and `gssrdoc` packages by running the code below:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages('gssr', repos =
  c('https://kjhealy.r-universe.dev', 'https://cloud.r-project.org'))

install.packages('gssrdoc', repos =
  c('https://kjhealy.r-universe.dev', 'https://cloud.r-project.org'))

```

Then you'll want to run the code below to set up your data for analysis.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(srvyr)
library(survey)
library(gssr)
library(gssrdoc)
library(haven)
gss<-gss_get_yr(year='2024')
wt_vars <- c("vpsu",     # PSU
             "vstrat",   # Strata          
             "wtssps",   # Weights
             "wtssnrps"  #  Weights with non-response adjustment
             )   

# removing user-missing values and converting the weights to numeric
gss<-gss|>
  zap_missing()|>
  mutate(across(wt_vars, .fns=~as.numeric(.x)))

```

```{r}

library(gssr)
library(dplyr)

data(gss_all, package = "gssr")   # loads the full object into memory

vars <- c("year", "age", "cohort", "sex", "race", "polviews", "partyid",
          "attend", "degree", "wtssall", "vstrat", "vpsu")

gss <- gss_all |>
  select(any_of(vars)) |>
  filter(year >= 2000) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(haven::zap_labels(.x))))

rm(gss_all); gc()   # free the big object right away
table(gss$year)
```

```{r}

library(gssr)
library(dplyr)

data(gss_all, package = "gssr")   # loads the full object into memory

vars <- c("year", "age", "cohort", "sex", "race", "polviews", "partyid",
          "attend", "degree", "wtssall", "vstrat", "vpsu")

gss <- gss_all |>
  select(any_of(vars)) |>
  filter(year >= 1972) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(haven::zap_labels(.x))))

rm(gss_all); gc()   # free the big object right away
table(gss$year)


library(ggplot2)
library(survey)
library(dplyr)

options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust") #this gets rid of the error that i kept getting

gss <- gss |> filter(!is.na(wtssall), !is.na(vpsu), !is.na(vstrat)) #Keeps only people who have a weight, a PSU, and a stratum
#making the generations,sex, and conservative/republican
gss <- gss |>
  mutate(
    generation = case_when(
      year - age >= 1997 ~ "Gen Z",
      year - age >= 1981 ~ "Millennial",
      year - age >= 1965 ~ "Gen X",
      year - age >= 1946 ~ "Boomer"),
    sex = factor(sex, labels = c("Men", "Women")),
    conservative = case_when(polviews >= 5 ~ 1, polviews %in% 1:4 ~ 0),
    republican   = case_when(partyid %in% 4:6 ~ 1, partyid %in% 0:3 ~ 0)
  )

#this accounts the survey design
des <- svydesign(ids = ~vpsu, strata = ~vstrat, weights = ~wtssall,
                 data = gss, nest = TRUE)

#Keep only ages 18-27 with a known generation
young <- subset(des, age >= 18 & age <= 27 & !is.na(generation))



# Percent conservative, by year and generation (ages 18-27)
yr_cons <- svyby(~conservative, ~year + generation, young, svymean, na.rm = TRUE)

#this plots for conservative
ggplot(yr_cons, aes(x = year, y = conservative * 100, color = generation)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = (conservative - 1.96 * se) * 100,
                    ymax = (conservative + 1.96 * se) * 100),
                width = 0.5, alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "Percent conservative among ages 18-27, by generation",
       x = "Survey year", y = "% conservative", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

# Percent republican, by year and generation (ages 18-27)
yr_rep  <- svyby(~republican,   ~year + generation, young, svymean, na.rm = TRUE)

#plot for republican
ggplot(yr_rep, aes(x = year, y = republican * 100, color = generation)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = (republican - 1.96 * se) * 100,
                    ymax = (republican + 1.96 * se) * 100),
                width = 0.5, alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "Percent Republican among ages 18-27, by generation",
       x = "Survey year", y = "% Republican", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

#this puts conservative and republican together
yr_all <- bind_rows(
  yr_cons |> rename(est = conservative) |> mutate(measure = "Conservative"),
  yr_rep  |> rename(est = republican)   |> mutate(measure = "Republican")
)

#plots both to show an overlap
ggplot(yr_all, aes(x = year, y = est * 100, color = generation, linetype = measure)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = (est - 1.96 * se) * 100,
                    ymax = (est + 1.96 * se) * 100),
                width = 0.5, alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "Conservative and Republican identification, ages 18-27, by generation",
       x = "Survey year", y = "Percent", color = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```
